items: ## 8\. Licensing and Professional Recognition

A bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering provides an academic foundation for engineering-related employment and further education. However, the requirements for working in a particular role depend on the employer, responsibilities, and country.

Mechanical engineering roles in private industry do not all require the same form of professional licensing. If you plan to work in a regulated position or move to another country after graduation, check the relevant local recognition and professional requirements.
Students planning to return to India should also review any requirements that apply to their intended employer, further studies, or specific professional role.
## 9\. Jobs and Salary After Mechanical Engineering in Finland
Graduates may explore opportunities across industrial and technology sectors, depending on their skills, experience, language ability, and work authorisation.
Potential career paths include:
Mechanical Design Engineer
Production Engineer
Manufacturing Engineer
CAD Engineer
Quality Control Engineer
Robotics or Mechatronics Engineer
Product Development Engineer
Maintenance Engineer
Research or Development Assistant
Employers may operate in manufacturing, automotive technology, industrial equipment, energy, automation, and product design.

Salary expectations: There is no single salary applicable to all graduates. Earnings depend on the role, employer, location, experience, and technical specialisation. Students should review current job advertisements and salary information before making career plans.
Graduates may also pursue a relevant master's degree to deepen their knowledge in mechanical engineering, materials science, mechatronics, industrial design, or another related discipline.
## 10\. Documents Required for Admission
Prepare the documents required by your selected university. These may include:
Valid passport.
Class 10 marksheet and certificate.
Class 12 marksheet and certificate.
Official academic transcripts.
Proof of English-language proficiency, if required.
SAT or other accepted test results, if applicable.
Certified translations of documents, where required.
Application forms and supporting declarations.
Any additional documents specified by the university.
Document requirements can vary. Always follow the official checklist for your chosen programme rather than assuming that every university asks for the same documents.
## 11\. Frequently Asked Questions
### 1\. Can Indian students study mechanical engineering in Finland after Class 12?

Yes. Indian students can apply to suitable bachelor's programmes if they meet the university's academic, language, and other admission requirements. The availability of English-taught programmes should be checked carefully.
### 2\. How long does a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering take in Finland?
A bachelor's degree commonly takes three years when the programme is structured around 180 ECTS credits. The exact duration depends on the course and degree pathway.
### 3\. What is the tuition fee for mechanical engineering in Finland?

Tuition fees vary by institution and programme. The identified LUT University mechanical engineering double-degree programme lists a fee of €12,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA students, approximately ₹13.03 lakh using the illustrative exchange rate above.
### 4\. Is IELTS compulsory for studying mechanical engineering in Finland?

Not necessarily. English-language requirements and accepted alternatives vary by university and programme. Applicants should check the official admission rules to determine whether IELTS or another form of proof is required.
### 5\. How can Edu-Hawk Worldwide help me apply?

Edu-Hawk Worldwide can guide students in shortlisting suitable programmes, understanding eligibility, organising application documents, and navigating the study-abroad application process. Admission decisions are made by the universities.
